title: Breath Acetone During Tirzepatide Treatment and Resistance Training in Adults With Obesity
official: Exhaled Breath Analysis for the Prediction of Treatment Response During Tirzepatide Therapy and Resistance Training in Adults With Obesity - An Ancillary Study to the RESIST Trial
summary: This study is an ancillary study to the RESIST trial, in which adults with obesity receive the weight-loss medication tirzepatide and are randomly assigned to a structured resistance training program or to usual care for 24 weeks. RESIST-EXHALE measures acetone in exhaled breath, a non-invasive marker of fat burning, at all seven RESIST visits (Week 0 to Week 24). The study investigates how breath acetone changes during treatment, whether this change differs between participants with and without resistance training, and whether breath acetone at the start or early in treatment can predict the individual response to treatment, such as weight loss and preservation of muscle. The measurement takes about 15-20 minutes at the first visit and about 10 minutes at each later visit. No additional visits, interventions or biological samples are part of this ancillary study.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Provisional eligibility for randomization into the RESIST trial (based on all RESIST screening assessments available at the time of informed consent for this ancillary study)
* Written informed consent for this ancillary study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Non-randomization into the RESIST trial for any reason
* Any anatomical or functional condition preventing breath sampling through a mouthpiece (e.g., tracheostomy, laryngectomy, severe facial deformity), such that a valid end-tidal breath sample cannot be obtained

Key eligibility criteria of the RESIST trial (for context only; full criteria see RESIST protocol RESIST-26-HAL-0150-I):

* Age 18-60 years
* Obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
* No manifest type 2 diabetes
* No structural cardiovascular disease
* Not pregnant or breastfeeding
* Sufficient command of the German language
